en: 5. The Chapter on Truths (Saccayamaka) 5.2 The Section on Occurrence (Pavattivāra) 5.2.1 The Section on Arising (Uppādavāra)
5.2.1.1. Chapter on the Present (Paccuppannavāra) 5.2.1.1.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom the truth of suffering arises, does the truth of the origin arise for that person?
For all those being reborn and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from craving,
the truth of suffering arises, but the truth of the origin does not arise for them. At the moment of the arising of craving, both the truth of suffering and the truth of the origin arise for them.
Or again, for whom origination-truth arises, for that person does suffering-truth arise? Yes.
For whom suffering-truth arises, for that person does path-truth arise?
For all those who are being reborn, and during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the path, for them suffering-truth [arises].

[It is] not that the truth of the path arises for them. In the five-aggregate realm, at the moment of the arising of the path, for those persons both the truth of suffering arises and the truth of the path arises.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path arises, does the truth of suffering arise for them?
In the formless realm, at the moment of the arising of the path, the truth of the path arises for them, but the truth of suffering does not arise for them.
In the five-aggregate realm, at the moment of the arising of the path, both the truth of the path and the truth of suffering arise for them.
Does the truth of the path arise for one for whom the truth of the origin arises? No.
Or rather, for whom the truth of the path arises, does the truth of the origin arise for that person? No.
5.2.1.1.2. Positive Spatial Analysis:
Where the truth of suffering arises, does the truth of the origin arise there?

In the case of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) arises there, but the truth of origination (*samudayasacca*) does not arise there. In the fourfold and fivefold planes of existence, both the truth of suffering and the truth of origination arise there. Or, conversely, where [the truth of origination arises]...? Yes.
Where the truth of suffering arises, does the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) arise there?

In the woeful states and among non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering arises there, but the truth of the path does not arise there. In the remaining four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms, both the truth of suffering and the truth of the path arise there.
Or rather, wherever the truth of the path arises, does the truth of suffering arise there? Yes.
Wherever the truth of the origin arises, does the truth of the path arise there?

In the woeful planes (apāya), the truth of the origin arises there, but the truth of the path does not arise there. In the remaining fourfold and fivefold planes, both the truth of the origin and the truth of the path arise there. Or, where [the truth of the path arises]...? Yes.
5.2.1.1.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom, wherever the truth of suffering arises, does the truth of the origin arise for them there?
… [The *yassa* and *yassayattha* sections should be expanded in the same manner. 5.2.1.1.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom suffering-truth does not arise, for that person does origination-truth not arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom origination-truth does not arise, for that person does suffering-truth not arise?
For all those being reborn, and during the course of existence at the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from craving—for them, origination-truth...
It does not arise, yet for them the truth of suffering does not fail to arise. For all those passing away, for those in the process of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness,
and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the path or the fruit,
neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of suffering arises.
Does the truth of suffering not arise for one for whom the truth of the path does not arise?
For those at the moment of the arising of the path in the formless realm, the truth of suffering does not arise; yet it is not the case that the truth of the path does not arise for them.
[This is true] for all those passing away, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the fruit in the formless realm.
For them, neither the truth of suffering nor the truth of the path arises.
Or rather: for whom the truth of the path does not arise, for that person does the truth of suffering not arise?
For all those being reborn, and during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the path, for them the truth of the path [does not arise].

It does not arise, yet for them the truth of suffering does not fail to arise. For all those passing away, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the fruit in the formless realm, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering arises.
Does the truth of the path not arise for one in whom the truth of the origin does not arise?
At the moment of the arising of the Path, origination-truth does not arise for them, but it is not the case that path-truth does not arise for them.
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from craving and dissociated from the Path,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, neither origination-truth nor path-truth arises.
Or, for whom path-truth does not arise, for them does origination-truth not arise?
At the moment of the arising of craving, path-truth does not arise for them, but origination-truth does not fail to arise for them.
[This is the case] for all at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from both the path and craving.

For those who have attained the cessation of perception and feeling (nirodhasamāpanna) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), neither the truth of the path (maggasacca) nor the truth of the origin (samudayasacca) arises.
5.2.1.1.5. Negative Spatial Analysis:
Where the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) does not arise, does the truth of the origin (samudayasacca) not arise there? There is no such case.
Or, where the truth of the origin does not arise, does the truth of suffering not arise there? It does arise.
Where the truth of suffering does not arise, does the truth of the path not arise there? There is none.
Or, where the truth of the path does not arise, does the truth of suffering not arise there? It does arise.
Where the truth of origination does not arise, does the truth of the path not arise there? Yes.
Or else, where the truth of the path does not arise, does the truth of origination not arise there?

In the woeful states, the truth of the path does not arise there, but the truth of origination does not fail to arise there. Among non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of origination arises there.
5.2.1.1.6. Negative Person-Space (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa) For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not arise, for that person there, origination-truth (samudayasacca) does not arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom, where origination-truth does not arise, for that person there, suffering-truth does not arise?

For all those being reborn, and at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from craving during the course of existence, origination-truth does not arise therein; yet it is not that suffering-truth does not arise therein for them.

For all those passing away, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the Path or the Fruit in the formless realm, [origination-truth does not arise] therein for them.
The truth of origination does not arise and the truth of suffering also does not arise.
For whom, where suffering does not arise, for them there does not arise the truth of the path?
In the immaterial realm (arūpa), at the moment of the arising of the path, for those [beings] there suffering does not arise; yet it is not that for them there [the truth of the path does not arise].

The truth of the path does not arise. For all those passing away, during the cessant phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the fruit—neither the truth of suffering nor the truth of the path arises in them there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever the truth of the path does not arise in a certain place, does the truth of suffering not arise for that person in that same place?
For all those being reborn, and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from the Path, the Truth of the Path does not arise therein;
yet it is not that the Truth of Suffering does not arise for them therein.

For all those passing away, and for those during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the Fruit [of the Path], the Truth of the Path does not arise therein...
The truth of suffering does not arise.
For whom, where the truth of origination does not arise, for them there, does the truth of the path not arise?
At the moment of the arising of the path, for those [beings], there the truth of origination does not arise; yet it is not the case that for them there [the truth of the path] does not arise.

The truth of the path does not arise. For all those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of the arising of a consciousness dissociated from craving and dissociated from the path, and for non-percipient beings—the truth of origination does not arise and the truth of the path also does not arise there.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever the truth of the path does not arise there, does the truth of origination not arise for them there?
At the moment of arising of craving, the truth of the path does not arise for them there, but the truth of the origin does not fail to arise for them there.
For all [beings] at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those at the moment of arising of a consciousness dissociated from both the path and craving,
and for non-percipient beings— the truth of the path does not arise for them there, nor does the truth of the origin arise.
5.2.1.2. Chapter on the Past (Atītavāra) 5.2.1.2.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) had arisen, for that person had the truth of origination (samudayasacca) arisen? Yes, it had.
Or, for whom the truth of origination had arisen, had the truth of suffering arisen for them? Yes.
For whom the truth of suffering had arisen, had the truth of the path arisen for them?

For those who have not yet fully realized [the truths], the truth of suffering had arisen, but the truth of the path had not arisen for them. For those who have fully realized [the truths], both the truth of suffering and the truth of the path had arisen.
Or for whomsoever... [as before] ...did it arise? Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of the origin (samudayasacca) had arisen, had the truth of the path (maggasacca) arisen for them?

For those who have not fully realized [the truths], the truth of the origin had arisen, but the truth of the path had not arisen for them. For those who have fully realized [the truths], both the truth of the origin and the truth of the path had arisen.
Or, for whom... [as before] ...did it arise? Yes. 5.2.1.2.2. Positive Plane:
Where the truth of suffering arose... [as before] ...did it arise? Yes.
(The *yatthaka* is identical in all respects. The differences in the sequence (*tanti*) are the same as in the previous *yatthaka*. 5.2.1.2.3.
Positive Person-Space Analysis For whom, wherever, the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) had arisen, for that person, there, had the truth of the origin (*samudayasacca*) arisen?
When the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes is occurring, for those non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering has arisen there,
but the truth of origination has not arisen for them there. For others— those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—
both the truth of suffering and the truth of origination have arisen there.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever [the path-truth] had arisen …pe… had it arisen? Yes.
For whomsoever and wherever the truth of suffering had arisen, had the truth of the path arisen for them there?

For those in the second moment of consciousness of the Pure Abodes, for those who have not yet fully realized [the truths], and for non-percipient beings—for them, there [the path-truth had not arisen].

The truth of suffering had arisen for them, but the truth of the path had not arisen for them there. For those who have fully realized [the truths], both the truth of suffering and the truth of the path had arisen there.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever ... pe ... had they arisen? Yes.
For whom, and in what [sphere], had the truth of origination arisen, for them had the truth of the path arisen there?

For those pure-abode beings while a second unwholesome consciousness was occurring, and for those who have not yet fully realized [the truths], the truth of origination had arisen there, but the truth of the path had not arisen there for them. For those who have fully realized [the truths], for them there...
The truth of origination arose and the truth of the path also arose.
Or rather, for whom and where [did they arise]? ...pe... Did they arise? Yes. 5.2.1.2.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala).
For whom suffering-truth had not arisen, had origination-truth not arisen for them?
None. Or again, for whom... [as before] ...had not arisen?
None. For whom suffering-truth had not arisen, had path-truth not arisen for them? None.
Or, for whom path-truth had not arisen, had suffering-truth not arisen for them? It had arisen.
For whom origin-truth had not arisen, had path-truth not arisen for them? There is none. Or, for whom...
[as before] ...had not arisen? It had arisen.
5.2.1.2.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering has not arisen … [etc. … 5.2.1.2.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) had not arisen, for that person there, origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) had not arisen? Yes.
Or rather, for whom, where origination-truth had not arisen, for that person there, suffering-truth had not arisen?
For those in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) while their second consciousness is occurring, and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), for them there, origination-truth had not arisen.
And for them, the truth of suffering did not arise there. For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), neither the truth of origination nor the truth of suffering arose there.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering did not arise in a certain place, for that person the truth of the path did not arise there? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever the truth of the path had not arisen at a certain place, had the truth of suffering not arisen for them there?

For those in the second moment of consciousness of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), for those who have not yet fully realized the truths, and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), the truth of the path had not arisen there, but it is not the case that the truth of suffering had not arisen for them there. [This applies to] the Pure Abodes...
For those beings being reborn there, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering had arisen.
For whomsoever the truth of the origin had not arisen at a certain place, had the truth of the path also not arisen for them at that same place? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever the truth of the path had not arisen at a certain place, had the truth of the origin also not arisen for them at that same place?
When a second unwholesome consciousness is occurring in the Pure Abodes for those who have not yet fully realized [the truths], the truth of the path has not arisen for them there;
however, it is not the case that the truth of the origin has not arisen for them there.
When a second consciousness is occurring in the Pure Abodes, or for non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin has arisen for them there.
5.2.1.3. Chapter on the Future (Anāgatavāra) 5.2.1.3.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) will arise, for that person will origination-truth (samudayasacca) arise?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the highest path,
the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) will arise, but the truth of origination (samudayasacca) will not arise for them.
For others, both the truth of suffering and the truth of origination will arise.
Or again, for whomsoever... [as before] ... Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering will arise, will the truth of the path arise for him?
For those who possess the highest path (agga-maggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path.
The truth of suffering will arise for them, but the truth of the path will not arise for them. For one who, immediately after this consciousness,
will attain the supreme path, and for others who will attain the path, both the truth of suffering and the truth of the path will arise.
Or again, for whom [the truth of suffering] will arise …pe… [it is] so.
For whom the truth of origin will arise, will the truth of the path arise for them?
For those worldlings who will not attain the path, the truth of origin will arise, but [the truth of the path will not].
For those persons, the truth of the path will arise. For those who will attain the path, both the truth of the origin and the truth of the path will arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will arise, will the truth of the origin arise for that person?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness, the truth of the path will arise,
but the truth of the origin will not arise for them. For those who will attain the path, both the truth of the path and the truth of the origin will arise.
5.2.1.3.2. Positive Section (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering will arise …pe… 5.2.1.3.3.
Positive Section on Persons and Bases (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) will arise, for that person there, origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) will arise?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamagga), for Arahants, for those whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the highest path,
and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta)— for them, suffering-truth will arise there, but for them origination-truth will not arise there.
It will arise. For others—those in the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—both the truth of suffering and the truth of origination will arise there.
Or, for whomsoever the truth of origination will arise in a certain place … [as before] … it will arise? Yes.
For whomsoever suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) will arise in a certain place, for that person will path-truth (maggasacca) arise in that same place?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path,
and for those bound for states of misery (āpāyika) and non-percipient beings (asaññasatta)— for these, suffering-truth will arise there, but path-truth will not arise for them there.

It will arise. For whichever consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the supreme path (aggamagga), and for those others who will attain the path, both the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) and the truth of the path (maggasacca) will arise therein.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will arise in a certain place, will the truth of suffering also arise for them in that same place? Yes, it will.
For whom, where the truth of origination will arise, will the truth of the path arise there for them?

For those bound for the states of misery and for those worldlings who will not attain the path, the truth of origination will arise there, but the truth of the path will not arise there for them. For those who will attain the path...
For those persons, both the truth of origination and the truth of the path will arise there.
Or rather: for whomsoever the truth of the path will arise in a certain place, will the truth of origination also arise for that person in that same place?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after a particular state of consciousness, the truth of the path will arise for them in that [consciousness].
And for them, the truth of origination will not arise there. For those who will attain the path, both the truth of the path and the truth of origination will arise there. 5.2.1.3.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom suffering-truth will not arise, for that person will origination-truth not arise? Yes.
Or else, for whom origination-truth will not arise, for that person will suffering-truth not arise?
For those possessing the highest path (the Arahants), and for one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the highest path.

For those persons, the truth of origination will not arise, but it is not the case that for them the truth of suffering will not arise. For those possessing their final consciousness, neither the truth of origination nor the truth of suffering will arise.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering will not arise, for him the truth of the path will also not arise? Yes.
Or, for whom path-truth will not arise, for them will suffering-truth not arise?

For those possessing the supreme path (the Arahants) and for those worldlings who will not attain the path, path-truth will not arise, but for them suffering-truth will not fail to arise. [This is so] for those possessing their final consciousness.
For them, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering will arise.
For whom the truth of the origin will not arise, will the truth of the path not arise for them?
For those who, immediately after this consciousness, will attain the supreme path, the truth of the origin will not arise.
And yet, for them, the truth of the path will not fail to arise. For those who possess the supreme path (the Arahants), neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of the path will arise.
Or rather: for whomsoever the truth of the path will not arise, for that person will the truth of the origin not arise?
For those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, the truth of the path will not arise,
but it is not the case that the truth of the origin will not arise for them. For those who possess the supreme path and for Arahants,
neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin will arise.
5.2.1.3.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering will not arise … [etc. … 5.2.1.3.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) will not arise, for that person there, origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) will not arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom, where origination-truth will not arise, for that person there, suffering-truth will not arise?
For those possessing the supreme path (aggamagga), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the supreme path.
For non-percipient beings, the truth of origination will not arise there, but it is not the case that the truth of suffering will not arise for them there.
For those possessing their final consciousness, neither the truth of origination nor the truth of suffering will arise there.
For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) will not arise, for that person there, path-truth (maggasacca) will not arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom, where path-truth will not arise, for that person there, suffering-truth will not arise?

[It will not arise] for those possessing the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path, and for those destined for the states of misery (āpāyika).
For non-percipient beings, the truth of the path will not arise there, yet the truth of suffering will not fail to arise for them there.
For those possessing their final consciousness, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering will arise there.
If, for a certain person, the truth of the origin will not arise in a certain place, will the truth of the path also not arise for that person in that place?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness, the truth of origination will not arise therein,
but it is not the case that the truth of the path will not arise for them therein. For those possessing the supreme path, for Arahants, and for non-percipient beings,
neither the truth of origination nor the truth of the path will arise therein.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will not arise at a certain place, will the truth of the origin not also arise for them there?

For those bound for the states of misery and for those worldlings who will not attain the path, the truth of the path will not arise there, but it is not that the truth of the origin will not arise for them there. [This is so] for those possessing the supreme path and for Arahants.
For those non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin will arise there.
5.2.1.4. Chapter on the Present and the Past. 5.2.1.4.1.
Positive Person.
For whom the truth of suffering arises, for that person did the truth of the origin arise? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom the truth of the origin had arisen, for that person does the truth of suffering arise?
For all those passing away, during the cessation-moment of consciousness in the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the Path and the Fruit in the formless realm.
For them, the truth of origination had arisen, but the truth of suffering does not arise for them.
For all those being reborn and during the moment of the arising of consciousness in the course of existence, both the truth of origination had arisen and the truth of suffering arises.
For whom the truth of suffering arises, had the truth of the path arisen for them? For those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] and are being reborn.
In those at the moment of the arising of consciousness during the course of existence, the truth of suffering arises, but the truth of the path has not arisen for them.
For those who have realized [the truths] and are being reborn, as well as for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness during the course of existence,
both the truth of suffering arises and the truth of the path has arisen.
Or, for whom the truth of the path had arisen, does the truth of suffering arise for them?

For those who have fully realized [the truths] at the moment of death, during the subsistence phase of the mind in the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the path and its fruit—
the truth of the path had arisen for them, but the truth of suffering does not arise for them.
For those who have realized the truths and are being reborn, and for those during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence,
both the truth of the path has arisen and the truth of suffering is arising. For whom the truth of the origin is arising, has the truth of the path arisen for them?
In those who have not yet realized [the truths], at the moment craving arises, the truth of the origin arises,
but the truth of the path has not arisen for them. In those who have realized [the truths], at the moment craving arises,
both the truth of the origin arises and the truth of the path has arisen for them.
Or again, for one in whom the truth of the path has arisen, does the truth of the origin arise?

For those who have fully realized [the truths], at the moment of the dissolution of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for those who have attained cessation—though the truth of the path has arisen for them, the truth of the origin does not arise for them. For those who have fully realized...
At the moment of the arising of craving, for those [beings], both the truth of the path has arisen and the truth of the origin is arising.
5.2.1.4.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Wherever the truth of suffering arises …pe… (All [sections] regarding the plane are identical.)
5.2.1.4.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-Puggalokāsa) For whom, where the truth of suffering arises, does the truth of origination have arisen there?

For those born in the Pure Abodes at the moment of the arising of the rebirth-consciousness, and for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings—at these places, [the truth of origination has not arisen].
The truth of suffering arises, but the truth of origination has not arisen for them there. For others—
those being reborn in the four- or five-aggregate realms— and during the moment of the arising of consciousness in the course of existence,
both the truth of suffering and the truth of origination arise for them there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) had arisen at a certain place, does suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) arise for them at that same place?
For those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence (pavatta),
and for those in the formless plane at the moment of the arising of the Path or the Fruit— origination-truth had arisen for them at that place, but suffering-truth does not arise for them there.

The truth of suffering arises. For those being reborn in the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms, at the moment of the arising of consciousness during the course of existence, both the truth of the origin and the truth of suffering have arisen for them there.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering arises in a particular place, has the truth of the path arisen for them in that same place?

At the moment of arising of the rebirth-consciousness of the Pure Abodes; at the moment of arising of consciousness during the course of existence for those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] while being reborn;
and at the moment of arising of consciousness for those being reborn as non-percipient beings—suffering-truth arises for them there, but path-truth had not previously arisen for them there.
For those who have fully realized [the truths] while being reborn, and during the course of existence...
At the moment of arising of consciousness, both the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) and the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) arise therein for those [beings].
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path has arisen in a certain place, does the truth of suffering arise for them there?

[It does not] for those who have already realized [the truths] at the moment of death, nor during the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, nor in the formless realm (*arūpa*) regarding the path and its fruition.
And at the moment of arising, for those [beings], the truth of the path (maggasacca) had arisen there, but the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) does not arise there for them.
For those who have fully realized [the truths] at the moment of rebirth, and during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness,
both the truth of the path had arisen there and the truth of suffering arises there.
For whom and where the truth of origination arises, for them has the truth of the path arisen there?

For those who have not yet fully realized [the truths], at the moment craving arises, the truth of origination arises for them there, but the truth of the path has not arisen for them there. For those who have fully realized [the truths], at the moment craving arises...
In that case, both the truth of origination (*samudayasacca*) arises and the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) has arisen.
Or rather: for whomsoever, wherever the truth of the path has arisen, does the truth of origination arise for them there?
[Answer: For those who have fully realized [the truths], at the moment of the dissolution of craving (*taṇhā*), while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, for them there—

The truth of the path had arisen for them, but the truth of the origin does not arise for them there. For those who have fully realized [the truths], at the moment craving arises, both the truth of the path and the truth of the origin have arisen and do arise for them there.
5.2.1.4.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom suffering-truth does not arise, for that person has origination-truth not arisen?
It has arisen.
Or rather, for whom origination-truth has not arisen, for that person does suffering-truth not arise? There is none.
For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not arise, for them has path-truth (maggasacca) not arisen?

For those who have fully realized [the truths] at the moment of death, during the subsistence phase of consciousness, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the path and its fruit—
for these, suffering-truth does not arise, yet path-truth has not failed to have arisen for them.
For those who have not yet attained realization and are passing away, and for those during the dissolution phase of the mind in the course of existence,

the truth of suffering does not arise and the truth of the path has also not arisen. Or conversely, for whomsoever the truth of the path has not arisen, does the truth of suffering not arise for them?

For those who have not yet attained realization (anabhisametāvī) at the moment of rebirth, and during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence (pavatta), the truth of the path (maggasacca) has not arisen,
but it is not the case that the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) does not arise for them. For those who have not yet attained realization at the moment of death,
and during the dissolution phase of consciousness in the course of existence, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering has arisen.
For whom origination-truth does not arise, for them path-truth has not arisen?

For those who have already realized [the truths], at the moment of the cessation of craving, when a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for those who have attained cessation—origination-truth does not arise for them, yet path-truth has not failed to arise for them. For those who have not yet realized [the truths]...
At the moment of the cessation of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings,
neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of the path has arisen.
Or, conversely, for whom the truth of the path has not arisen, does the truth of the origin not arise for them?
For those who have not yet attained realization, at the moment craving arises, the truth of the path has not arisen for them,
but the truth of the origin does not fail to arise for them. For those who have not yet attained realization, at the moment craving ceases,
when a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin has arisen.
5.2.1.4.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering does not arise … [etc. … 5.2.1.4.6.
Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not arise, for them there, origination-truth (samudayasacca) has not arisen?
For those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate planes, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence,
and for those in the formless plane at the moment of the arising of the Path or the Fruit— there, suffering-truth does not arise, yet for them there [origination-truth] has not [necessarily] arisen.

The truth of origination had not arisen for them. For those in the pure abodes at the moment of the dissolution of the rebirth-consciousness, and for those passing away from the non-percipient beings, neither the truth of suffering nor the truth of origination has arisen there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever the truth of origination had not arisen in a certain place, does the truth of suffering not arise for that person in that same place?

At the moment of the arising of the rebirth-consciousness of those born in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), and for those beings of the non-percipient realm (asaññasatta) who are being reborn, the truth of origination (samudayasacca) has not arisen there;
yet it is not the case that the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) does not arise there for them.

At the moment of the dissolution of the rebirth-consciousness of those born in the Pure Abodes, and for those beings of the non-percipient realm who are passing away, the truth of origination... [does not arise there].
The truth of suffering has not arisen, and the truth of suffering does not arise.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering does not arise at a certain place, for that person the truth of the path has not arisen at that place?
[It is so] for those who have fully realized [the truths] at the moment of death, during the subsistence phase of consciousness, and in the formless realm, regarding both the path and its fruit.
And at the moment of arising, suffering-truth does not arise for them there, but path-truth has not failed to arise for them there.
For those in the death-moment of the rebirth-consciousness of pure-abode beings, for those dying who have not yet fully realized [the truths],
for those in the death-moment of the mind during the course of existence, and for those dying as non-percipient beings— suffering-truth [does not arise] for them there...
Does the truth of the path not arise, and has it also not arisen?
Or, conversely, for whomsoever and wherever the truth of the path has not arisen, does the truth of suffering not arise for them there? [Answer:

At the moment of the arising of the rebirth-consciousness of those in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), and during the course of existence (pavatta) for those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] while being reborn.
At the moment of the arising of consciousness in those beings reborn in the non-percipient realm,

path-truth had not arisen there for them, yet suffering-truth does not fail to arise there for them. [This is also the case] at the moment of the dissolution of the rebirth-consciousness of pure-abode beings,
for those who are not yet fully enlightened at the time of death, during the course of existence at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those dying from the non-percipient realm.
For them, in that case, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering had arisen.
For whom, in what place, the truth of the origin does not arise—for them, in that place, had the truth of the path not arisen?
[Answer: For those who have fully realized [the truths], at the moment of the cessation of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring—in them, in that case...
The truth of origination does not arise for them there, but it is not the case that the truth of the path had not previously arisen for them there.
For those in the second moment of consciousness in the Pure Abodes, for those who have not yet fully realized the truths at the moment of the cessation of craving,
for those in a consciousness dissociated from craving, and for non-percipient beings— the truth of origination does not arise and the truth of the path had also not previously arisen for them there.
Or, for whomsoever the truth of the path (maggasacca) had not arisen at a certain place, does the truth of the origin (samudayasacca) not arise for them there?
For those who have not yet fully realized [the truths] (anabhisametāvī) at the moment of the arising of craving (taṇhā), the truth of the path had not arisen there;

yet, for them, the truth of the origin does not fail to arise there. Also, for those in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) when their second consciousness is occurring, and for those who have not yet fully realized [the truths].

At the moment of the dissolution of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings—therein, both the truth of the path has not arisen and the truth of the origin does not arise. 5.2.1.5.
Chapter on the Present and Future.
5.2.1.5.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) arises, will origination-truth (samudayasacca) arise for that person?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants, and for the consciousness immediately following which [the path arises]...
At the moment of arising of that consciousness for those who will attain the highest path, the truth of suffering arises,
but the truth of origination will not arise for them. For others, at the moment of rebirth and during the course of existence at the moment of arising of consciousness,
both the truth of suffering arises and the truth of origination will arise.
Or, for whom origination-truth (samudayasacca) will arise, for them suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) arises?

For all those passing away, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of the path or the fruit—origination-truth will arise for them, but suffering-truth does not arise for them. For all those being reborn...
In the process [of consciousness], at the moment of the arising of the mind, both the truth of the origin (*samudayasacca*) will arise and the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) arises.
For whom the truth of suffering arises, will the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) arise for them?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (*aggamagga*), at the moment of the arising of the mind of Arahants, and for those worldlings (*puthujjana*) who have not yet attained the path...

For those who will not obtain [the path], at the moment of their rebirth and during the arising-phase of the mind in the course of existence (*pavatta*), the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) arises,
but the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) will not arise for them. For that mind immediately after which they will obtain the supreme path (*aggamagga*),
and for others who will obtain the path, at the moment of the arising of that mind—

For those who are being reborn and for those at the moment of the arising of consciousness during the course of existence, both the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) arises and the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) will arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will arise, does the truth of suffering arise for them?
For one who will attain the supreme path immediately after a particular state of consciousness—at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness, and for those...
For others who will attain the path, at the moment of their death, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during its course,
and at the moment of the arising of the path and the fruit in the formless realm, the truth of the path will arise for them,
but the truth of suffering does not arise for them. For that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path...
At the moment of arising of consciousness in one who will attain the Path, in those being reborn, and during the course of existence at the moment of arising of consciousness—
will the Truth of the Path arise and the Truth of Suffering also arise for them?
For whom the Truth of Origination arises, will the Truth of the Path arise for them?
In those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, at the moment of the arising of craving, the truth of origination arises,
but the truth of the path will not arise for them. In those who will attain the path,
at the moment of the arising of craving, both the truth of origination arises and the truth of the path will arise.
Or rather, for whom path-truth will arise, for that person does origination-truth arise?
For those who, immediately after this consciousness, will attain the highest path; for others who will attain the path at the moment of the dissolution of craving;
for those in whom a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring; for those who have entered cessation-attainment; and for non-percipient beings.

For those persons, the truth of the path will arise, but the truth of the origin does not arise for them. For those who will attain the path at the moment of the arising of craving, both the truth of the path and the truth of the origin will arise for them. 5.2.1.5.2.
Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Where the truth of suffering arises …pe… (The "where" section [yatthaka] should also be constructed in the same manner as the "for whom" section [yassakatthaka]).
5.2.1.5.3. Positive Person and Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom, and where, does the truth of suffering arise, will for that person and in that place the truth of the origin arise?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path; at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants;
at the moment of the arising of the consciousness immediately preceding those who will attain the supreme path; and for those reborn in the realm of non-percipient beings.
For them, the truth of suffering arises there, but the truth of origination will not arise for them there. For others—
those being reborn in the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms, and during the moment of the arising of consciousness in the course of existence—
the truth of suffering arises there and the truth of origination will also arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever origination-truth (*samudayasacca*) will arise at a certain place, does suffering-truth (*dukkhasacca*) arise for them at that same place?
For those passing away from the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms during the cessant phase of a consciousness in the course of existence,
and for those at the nascent phase of the path or the fruit in the formless realm— origination-truth will arise for them there, but suffering-truth does not arise for them there.

The truth of suffering arises. For those being reborn in the four-aggregate or five-aggregate realms, at the moment of the arising of consciousness during the course of existence, both the truth of the origin and the truth of suffering will arise there.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering arises in a particular place, will the truth of the path arise for them in that same place?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants, for those bound for the states of misery,
for those worldlings who will not attain the path at the moment of rebirth, and during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness—
for these, the truth of suffering arises there, but the truth of the path does not arise there for them.
It will arise. At the moment of arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path,
and for those others who will attain the path at the moment of their rebirth, and during the course of existence at the moment of arising of their consciousness—
therein, both the truth of suffering arises and the truth of the path will arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever the Truth of the Path will arise at a certain place, does the Truth of Suffering arise for that person at that place?
For one who will attain the Supreme Path immediately after a particular moment of consciousness— at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness—
and for others who will attain the Path while passing away, as well as during the moment of the dissolution of the consciousness in the course of existence in the formless realm (arūpa).
At the moment of the arising of the path and its fruit, the truth of the path will arise for them there,
but the truth of suffering does not arise for them there. For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after a particular state of consciousness,
at the moment of the arising of that consciousness, as well as for others who will attain the path at the moment of rebirth—
In the case of those whose consciousness is in the process of arising, the truth of the path will arise there and the truth of suffering is also arising there.
For whom, where the truth of the origin arises, will the truth of the path arise there?
[It will] for those born in the states of deprivation and for those worldlings who will not attain the path, at the moment of the arising of craving.
For them, the truth of the origin arises there, but the truth of the path will not arise for them there.
For those who will attain the path at the moment of the arising of craving,
both the truth of the origin arises there and the truth of the path will arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of the path will arise at a certain place, does the truth of the origin arise for them at that same place?
For those who will attain the highest path immediately after a particular moment of consciousness,
and for others who will attain the path— at the moment of the dissolution of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring— for them, the truth of the path [will arise] there.

[Craving] will arise for them there, but the truth of origination does not arise for them there. For those who will attain the path, at the moment craving arises for them, both the truth of the path and the truth of origination arise for them there. 5.2.1.5.4.
Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala).
For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not arise, for them will origination-truth (samudayasacca) not arise?

For all those passing away, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the Path and the Fruit in the formless realm—suffering-truth does not arise for them, yet origination-truth will not fail to arise for them. [This holds true] for the Supreme Path...
At the moment of the cessation of the consciousness of Arahants; at the moment of the cessation of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the highest path;

at the moment of the arising of the highest path and its fruit in the formless realm—at these times, neither the truth of suffering nor the truth of the origin arises, nor will the truth of the origin arise for them.
Or, for whom origination-truth will not arise, for that person does suffering-truth not arise?
At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants,
and at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path— for these, origination-truth will not arise.

And yet, the truth of suffering does not fail to arise for them. For those at the moment of the cessation of the supreme path (aggamagga), for Arahants at the moment of the cessation of consciousness,
for those who will attain the supreme path immediately after a particular state of consciousness at the moment of its cessation,
and for those in the formless realm at the moment of the arising of both the supreme path and its fruition— for all these, neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of suffering will arise.
And the truth of suffering does not arise.
For whom the truth of suffering does not arise, will the truth of the path not arise for them?
For one who will attain the supreme path immediately after a particular moment of consciousness—at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness, for those...

For others who will attain the path, at the moment of their death, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the path and the fruit in the formless realm, suffering-truth does not arise for them; yet it is not the case that path-truth will not arise for them.
At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path, at the moment of the cessation of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those...
For those ordinary persons who will not attain the path at the moment of their death, or during the subsistence phase of consciousness in the formless realm,
or at the moment of the arising of the highest path and its fruit— suffering-truth does not arise for them, and path-truth will not arise. Or conversely,
for whom path-truth will not arise, does suffering-truth not arise for them?

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path (agga-magga), at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path at the moment of rebirth and during the course of existence at the moment of the arising of consciousness—path-truth (maggasacca) will not arise for them;
yet, suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) does not fail to arise for them. [This also applies] at the moment of the dissolution of the supreme path for Arahants.
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness in those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, at the moment of death of those [ordinary persons],
at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness during the course of existence, and at the moment of the arising of the highest path and its fruit in the formless realm—
for these, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering will arise.
For whom origination-truth does not arise, for that person will path-truth not arise?
For one whose consciousness is immediately followed by the attainment of the supreme path; for others who will attain the path;
at the moment of the dissolution of craving in those [persons]; when a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring; for those who have attained cessation; and for non-percipient beings.
For them, the truth of the origin does not arise, yet it is not the case that for them the truth of the path will not arise.
For those possessing the highest path (the Arahants), for those ordinary persons who will not attain the path,
and for those at the moment of the dissolution of craving while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring— for these, neither the truth of the origin nor the truth of the path will arise.
Or, for whom path-truth will not arise, for them does origination-truth not arise?

For those worldlings who will not attain the path—at the moment of the arising of their craving—path-truth will not arise for them, yet origination-truth does not fail to arise for them. [This is not the case] for those possessing the supreme path (arahants).

And for those worldlings who will not attain the path, at the moment of the cessation of craving (*taṇhā*)—while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring—the truth of the path will not arise, and the truth of the origin does not arise. 5.2.1.5.5.

Where the truth of suffering does not arise … [etc.

For whom, where the truth of suffering does not arise, will the truth of the origin not arise there?
For those passing away from the four- or five-aggregate planes, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence,
and for those in the formless plane at the moment of the arising of the Path or the Fruit— suffering-truth does not arise there for them, yet origination-truth will not fail to arise for them there.
[This is also the case] at the moment of the cessation of the Supreme Path and at the moment of the cessation of the consciousness of Arahants.
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after that consciousness—at the moment of the dissolution of that consciousness; for those passing away from the non-percipient beings;
and for those at the moment of the arising of the supreme path and its fruit in the formless realm—the truth of suffering does not arise there, nor will the truth of origination arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever origination-truth will not arise at a certain place, does suffering-truth not arise for that person at that place?
[It does not arise] at the moment of the arising of the supreme path (aggamagga), at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants,
at the moment of the arising of that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the supreme path, and for those being reborn in the realm of non-percipient beings.
For them, the truth of origination will not arise there, but it is not the case that the truth of suffering does not arise for them there.

At the moment of the cessation of the supreme path; at the moment of the cessation of the consciousness of Arahants; at the moment of the cessation of that consciousness immediately after which one will attain the supreme path;
and in the formless realm, at the moment of the cessation of the supreme path and its fruition.
And for those at the moment of rebirth-linking, for those born in the non-percipient realm, and for those passing away from the non-percipient realm,
neither the truth of origination nor the truth of suffering will arise there.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering does not arise in a certain place, will the truth of the path not arise for them in that same place?
At the moment of dissolution of that consciousness after which they will attain the supreme path;
at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness of others who will attain the path while passing away; at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness during the course of existence;
and at the moment of the arising of the path and its fruit in the formless realm—for these persons, suffering-truth does not arise there, yet it is not the case that...
For them, the truth of the path will not arise there. This is the case at the moment of the cessation of the supreme path (agga-magga),

for Arahants at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, for those bound for the states of misery (āpāyika), for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path at the moment of their death,

for those in the course of existence at the moment of the cessation of consciousness, for those non-percipient beings (asaññasatta) at the moment of their death, and for those in the formless realm (arūpa) at the moment of the cessation of the supreme path and its fruition.
And at the moment of arising, neither the truth of suffering nor the truth of the path arises for them there.
Or rather: for whomsoever the truth of the path will not arise in a certain place, does the truth of suffering not arise for them there? [It does not.

At the moment of the arising of the supreme path, at the moment of the arising of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those subject to rebirth in the woeful states, as well as for those worldlings—

For those who will not attain the path at the moment of rebirth, during the arising phase of consciousness in the course of existence, and for those being reborn among the non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), the truth of the path (*maggasacca*) will not arise there;
yet it is not the case that the truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*) does not arise for them there.

[This is also the case] at the moment of the cessation of the supreme path (*agga-magga*), at the moment of the cessation of the consciousness of Arahants, and for those bound for the states of deprivation (*āpāyika*).
And for those worldlings who will not attain the path, at the moment of their death, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness during the course of existence,
at the moment of the arising of the highest path and its fruit in the formless realm, and for those non-percipient beings at the moment of their death— therein,
neither the truth of the path nor the truth of suffering will arise.
For whom and where the truth of origination does not arise, for that person and in that place, will the truth of the path not arise?
For those who will attain the supreme path immediately after this consciousness,
and for others who will attain the path— at the moment of the dissolution of craving, while a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring— for them, in that place, the truth of origination...
It does not arise, yet for them the truth of the path will not fail to arise there. For those possessing the highest path (arahants), for those bound for the states of deprivation,
and for those worldlings who will not attain the path— at the moment of the cessation of craving,
when a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings— for these, neither does the truth of the origin arise there.
And the truth of the path will not arise.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever the truth of the path will not arise, does the truth of the origin not arise for them there? [It does not.
For those bound for the states of misery (āpāyika) and for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path at the moment of the arising of craving.
For them, the truth of the path will not arise there, but it is not the case that the truth of the origin does not arise for them there.

[This is true] for those possessing the highest path, for Arahants, for those bound for the states of deprivation, and for those worldlings who will not attain the path— at the moment of the dissolution of craving,
when a consciousness dissociated from craving is occurring, and for non-percipient beings— for these, the truth of the path will not arise there.
The truth of the path will not arise and the truth of the origin does not arise.
5.2.1.6. Chapter on the Past and Future. 5.2.1.6.1.
Positive Person-Sequence.
For whom suffering-truth (dukkhasacca) has arisen, will origination-truth (samudayasacca) arise for them?

For those possessing the supreme path (aggamaggasamaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following which they will attain the supreme path—for these, suffering-truth has arisen, but origination-truth will not arise for them. For others...
For those persons, both the truth of suffering has arisen and the truth of origination will arise.
Or rather, for whomsoever the truth of origination will arise, has the truth of suffering arisen for them? Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of suffering has arisen, will the truth of the path arise for them?
For those possessing the highest path (aggamagga), for Arahants, and for those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path,
the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) has arisen, but the truth of the path (maggasacca) will not arise for them. For that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the highest path,
and for others who will attain the path, both the truth of suffering and the truth of the path have arisen.
And the truth of the path will arise.
Or for whomsoever... [etc.]? Yes.
For whomsoever the truth of the origin had arisen, will the truth of the path arise for him? Not for those who possess the supreme path (agga-magga).
For Arahants and for those ordinary persons who will not attain the path, the truth of the origin has arisen,
but the truth of the path will not arise for them. For that consciousness immediately after which they will attain the supreme path,
and for others who will attain the path, both the truth of the origin has arisen and the truth of the path will arise.
Or for whomsoever... [as before] ...? Yes. 5.2.1.6.2.
Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa):
Where the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) has arisen... [as before] ...?
5.2.1.6.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-puggalokāsa) For whom, where suffering-truth (dukkha-sacca) has arisen, will origination-truth (samudaya-sacca) arise there?
[It will arise] for those possessing the supreme path (aggamagga-samaṅgī), for Arahants, and for those whose consciousness immediately following [whichever] mind they will attain the supreme path.
For non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering has arisen there, but the truth of origination will not arise there for them.
For others— those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms— both the truth of suffering has arisen there and the truth of origination will arise there.
Or, for whomsoever origination-truth will arise at a certain place, has suffering-truth arisen there for them?

For those being reborn in the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), origination-truth will arise there, but suffering-truth had not arisen there for them. For others—those of the four-aggregate and five-aggregate realms—[both will arise].
The truth of origination will arise and the truth of suffering has arisen.
For whom, where suffering has arisen, will the truth of the path arise there for them?
[It will not arise] for those possessing the supreme path (arahants), for worldlings who will not attain the path, and for those bound for the states of misery.
For non-percipient beings, the truth of suffering has arisen there, but the truth of the path will not arise there for them.
For those who, immediately after this consciousness, will attain the supreme path,
and for others who will attain the path, both the truth of suffering has arisen there and the truth of the path will arise there.
Or, for whomsoever the Truth of the Path will arise at a certain place, had the Truth of Suffering already arisen for them there?
For those beings being reborn in the Pure Abodes (Suddhāvāsa), the Truth of the Path will arise there, but the Truth of Suffering had not already arisen for them there.
For one whose consciousness immediately precedes the attainment of the Supreme Path (Aggamagga), and for others...
For those who will attain the path, the truth of the path will arise there and the truth of suffering has arisen there.
For whomsoever the truth of the origin has arisen at a certain place, will the truth of the path arise for them at that same place? [No;
for those possessing the supreme path (arahants), for ordinary persons who will not attain the path, and for those bound for the states of loss.
For them, the truth of origination had arisen there, but the truth of the path will not arise there for them.
For those who, immediately after that consciousness, will attain the supreme path, and for others who will attain the path,
both the truth of origination had arisen there and the truth of the path will arise there.
Or, for whomsoever the truth of the path will arise at a certain place, had the truth of the origin arisen for them there?
For those in the second consciousness of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa), the truth of the path will arise there, but the truth of the origin had not arisen for them there.
[This is also the case] for one who, immediately after that consciousness, will attain the supreme path (aggamagga).
And for those others who will attain the path, both the truth of the path and the truth of the origin will arise therein; [but] the truth of the origin has already arisen [for them]. 5.2.1.6.4.
Negative Person: For whom the truth of suffering has not arisen, will the truth of the origin not arise for them? There is none.
Or, for whom the truth of origination will not arise, for that person did the truth of suffering not arise? It did arise.
For whom the truth of suffering did not arise, for that person will the truth of the path not arise?
There is no such case. Or, for whom the truth of the path will not arise, for that person did the truth of suffering not arise? It did arise.
For whom origination-truth had not arisen, for that person will path-truth not arise? None.
Or else, for whom path-truth will not arise, for that person had origination-truth not arisen? It had arisen.
5.2.1.6.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where the truth of suffering has not arisen … [as before] … 5.2.1.6.6.
Negative Person-Plane (Paccanīka-Puggalokāsa):
For whom, where the truth of suffering has not arisen, will the truth of origination not arise there? It will arise.
Or again, for whomsoever origination-truth will not arise at a certain place, has suffering-truth not arisen there for them? It has arisen.
For whomsoever suffering-truth has not arisen at a certain place, will path-truth not arise there for them? It will arise.
Or again, for whomsoever path-truth will not arise at a certain place, has suffering-truth not arisen there for them? It has arisen.
For whom, where origination-truth has not arisen, will path-truth not arise there?

For those in the second moment of consciousness among the Pure Abodes, origination-truth has not arisen there, yet path-truth will not fail to arise there for them. For non-percipient beings, both origination-truth and...
[The truth of the path] had not arisen and will not arise.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever the truth of the path will not arise, for that person there, had the truth of the origin not already arisen?
[It had not arisen] for those possessing the supreme path (agga-magga), for Arahants, for those worldlings who will not attain the path, and for those destined for the states of misery (āpāyika).
For them, the truth of the path will not arise there, but it is not the case that for them the truth of the origin did not arise there.
For non-percipient beings, neither the truth of the path nor the truth of the origin will arise there, nor did they arise there.
